label: late copy-phase steps of length-9 sequences with input p/d/o/f/i/r
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and never at recall_idx 0. Within the copy phase it prefers fed-back inputs p (about 12x lift, 41% of mass), then d, o and f (about 4-5x each), with weaker i and r; phase==2 plus one of p/d/o/f covers 80% of the mass but has only 4% precision. Rate and mass climb sharply toward the end of long sequences: L=9 holds 78% of the mass, and t=16-17 (the last two outputs of L=9) hold 55%. The top activations are p/d/f/o inputs at the final copy steps of 9-token sequences. The chosen predicate (copy phase, t>=16, input in {p,d,o,f,i,r}) has precision of only about 0.18 and mass recall of about 0.47 on dev. Most steps matching the description stay below threshold, and there is a diffuse tail of weak activations at earlier copy steps and with shorter L. Magnitudes are tiny overall (max 0.005).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=11: p, d, f, o; t=17: p, o, f, d; t=12: p, d, f, o) and the token being output (most: o, i, p, m, 3, r; least: q, w, e, y); timing cues that raise it most: t=17, recall_idx=8, L=9 & t=17.
